definitions.explanation: A Buddhist temple, used with the polite prefix お. The standard everyday form when referring to temples in conversation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お{寺|てら}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There are many temples in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: ⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧お{寺|てら}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{参|まい}り→お参り：16837_omairi⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I visited a temple with my family.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧お{寺|てら}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{桜|さくら}→桜：02212_sakura⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{名所|めいしょ}→名所：08164_meisho⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧だ。
examples.english: That temple is famous as a cherry blossom viewing spot.

notes:
The polite form of ⟦{寺|てら}→寺：01676_tera⟧, using the honorific prefix お. In everyday conversation, お{寺|てら} is much more common than the plain form ⟦{寺|てら}→寺：01676_tera⟧. The お prefix is not strictly honorific here — it has become a natural part of the word in spoken Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{寺|てら}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go to a temple
- お{寺|てら}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{参|まい}り→お参り：16837_omairi⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to visit a temple (for worship)
- お{寺|てら}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{回|まわ}る→回る：01150_mawaru⟧: to visit several temples
- お{寺|てら}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧: a temple bell

TEMPLE VS. SHRINE:
- お{寺|てら}: Buddhist temple — features a ⟦{本堂|ほんどう}→本堂：15935_hondou⟧ (main hall), ⟦{仏像|ぶつぞう}→仏像：09638_butsuzou⟧ (Buddha statues), and often a ⟦{墓地|ぼち}→墓地：15232_bochi⟧ (cemetery)
- ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧: Shinto shrine — features a ⟦{鳥居|とりい}→鳥居：05956_torii⟧ (torii gate) and ⟦{狛犬|こまいぬ}→狛犬：07115_komainu⟧ (guardian lion-dogs)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{寺院|じいん}→寺院：00122_jiin⟧: temple — a more formal, written-style word for Buddhist temples
- ⟦{寺|てら}→寺：01676_tera⟧: temple — the plain form, used mainly in compounds and written contexts
